2. The capacity tax was recognized by the Constitution (6th Amendment) Act, 1966 by addition of Item i) to Entry No. 43 of the Third Schedule to the Constitution of Pakistan, 1962. By this amendment the Central Legislature was authorized to make laws in respect of taxes and duties on the production Bangladesh and others capacity of any plant, machinery, undertaking, Respondents establishment or installation in lieu of taxes and duties the writ specified in any one or more items (b), (c) and (f) of Entry No. 43. 

 4. SRO No. 124 (Annexure-C in Writ Petition Nos. 838, 728 of 1990 and 1092/89, Annexure-B in 1115/89, 803, 802 of 1990 and Annexure-A in WP No. 456/89) dated 18.6.87, SR No. 192 dated 1.7.88 (Annexure-E (i) in WP Nos. 838, 728 of 1990, Annexure-B(I) in WP Nos. 802 and 803 of 1990) and SRO No. 204 dated 15.6.89 (Annexure-C(2) in WP No. 728/90 Annexure-B(2) in WP No.802 and 803/90 Annexure-C(3) in 838/90) were issued by the National Board of Revenue, By the SRO 124 dated 18.6.87 the respondent fixed the capacity and rate of excise duties on, item No. 02-03-Beverage-Aerated Waters, all sorts fixing 10 lacs bottle per filling valy per year as the capacity and also fixing T. 7 lacs as rate of each value of each year. By SRO No. 192 dated 1.7.88 fixing the capacity filing value to be 2 crores 50 lacs bottle and the rate was fixed at 80%, 64% and 48% for the Dhaka, Chittagong, Rajshahi and Khulna Divisions respectively per year and earlier SRO No.124 dated 18.6.87 was cancelled. Thereafter by another SRO being SRO No. 204 dated 15.6.89 the excise duty was further amended by inserting rule 4 fixing the rate at section (4) and sub-sections (5) (6) and (7) were added to section 3. Taka 2 crores 50 lacs for the Dhaka Division, Taka 2 crore for the Chittagong Division and Taka 1 crore 50 lacs for the Rajshahi and Khulna Divisions. The rate was further enhanced by SRO No. 240 dated 14.6.90 at Taka 3 crores 12 lacs for the Dhaka Division, Taka 2 crores 50 lacs for the Chittagong Division and Taka 1 crore 88 lacs for the Khulna and Rajshahi Divisions It is stated that the provisions of sub-sections (4), (5) and (6) or section 3 of the Excise and Salt Act, 1944 were amended but the provisions relating to levy and collections of duties on production capacity remained substantially the same. The expression "production capacity of plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments or installations" has been changed to "capacity of plants, machinery, undertakings, establishment or installations" and the reviewing body has been named as "Standing Tribunal" in place of "Review Board". It is stated that though the capacity of the petitioners’ plants are 16 million boules annually, the petitioners could not produce full capacity because of various reasons. In Writ Petition No. 728/90 the petitioner stated the production capacity and the duty paid as under: 

 Year Production 

 By the notification dated 18.6.87 the petitioners were required to pay fixed duty at Taka. 7 lacs per value at 1 million bottles annually and the petitioners were required to pay excise duty of Taka 3,36,00,000.00 for 4,80,00,000 bottles in a year although there was no special market value and the market demand was a little more than two million bottles per year. It is to be stated that no guiding principle was laid down for determination of such production capacity. The said notification dated 18.6.87 was substituted by subsequent notification namely, SRO No. 192 dated 1.7.88 where also no guiding principle for determination of capacity was specified and the capacity for each filling machine was fixed without any inquiry or Obtaining ,any necessary date aribtrarily. The said notification further provided that if the factory remained closed for specified reasons for 190 or more consecutive days, the assesse would be entitled to proportionate exemption of duty. Fixation of 190 days was also arbitrary and without any reasonable objective basis shown in the said SRO. 

 8. It is argued by Mr. Syed Ishtiaq Ahmed that the guiding principles are condition precedent for determination of production capacity under section 3 (4) of the Excise and Salt Act, 1944. The fixation of production capacity by Rules under the SROs which are under challenge arc highly illegal, arbitrary and oppressive, It is argued that the determination of production capacity by the impugned SROs without making any inquiry and obtaining necessary data and such determination being devoid of the idea of production in fact, the fixation of capacity, rate of levy and collection of excise duty are arbitrary and malafide. The aforesaid determination of capacity by the impugned notifications being arbitrary, oppressive and unreasonable the same are violative of fundamental right of the petitioners and as such are to be declared illegal and without any lawful authority, The same being also discriminatory as such are violative of Articles 27 and 31 of the Constitution. It is also argued by the learned Advocate that closure of the factory for 190 days without break is arbitrary as it tantamounts to right of exemption which the petitioners are entitled in accordance with law, as such, the same arc illegal and without lawful authority. It is further argued by the learned Advocate that delegation of power under section 3(4) of the Act to the Board to levy duty and to vary the levy which is an essential legislative function is also illegal and void as it constitutes excessive and impermissible legislative derogation of power, 

 10. We have heard the learned Advocates and also perused the petitions and affidavit filed by the respective parties. Indeed there is a noticable departure from the earlier levy of collection of excise duty. Before making amendment of sub-section (4) of section 3 the levy of duty on excisable goods were done according to actual production. A change from the levy of duty according to actual production to levy of duty according to production capacity introduces a new experiment in the fiscal field of levy and collection of excise duty. In the year of 1961 by amendment a new sub-section namely, sub-section (4) was added to section 3 of the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944. It provided that Central Government may in lieu of levying and collecting duties of excise on excisable goods under section 3(1), levy and collect, in such manner and at such rates as may be prescribed duties of excise on the plant and machinery, or a part thereof, manufacturing or producing excisable goods, In 1965, the Finance Act, 1965 amended sub-section (4) by adding the words "productive capacity or the" after the words "on the", In 1966 the Constitution (Sixth Amendment) Act, 1966 was passed which amended Entry No. 43 of the Third Schedule of the Constitution of Pakistan, 1962 by addition of item(l) thereto, by which the Central Legislature was given power to make laws providing for imposition of taxes and duties on the production capacity of any machinery, undertaking, establishment or installation in lieu of the duties specified in items (b) (c) and (f) of Entry No. 43. 

 11. Consequent upon this constitutional amendment, the Central Legislature by Finance Act, 1966 (X I of 1966), substituted sub-section (4) of section 3 and added new sub-sections (5), (6) (7) to section 3 of the Act which were further amended by Finance Ordinances 1969 and 1970. The amended provisions of the Act relating to the levy and collection of duty on production capacity of plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments or installations producing or manufacturing excisable goods in lieu of excise duty are reproduced as follows: 

 "4) With the prior approval of the Central Government, the Central Board of Revenue may, in lieu of levying and collecting under sub-section (I) duties of excise on excisable goods, by notification in the official Gazette, levy and collect duties on the production capacity of plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments or installations producing or manufacturing such goods; and such notifications shall specify. 

 (a) the guiding principles for the determination of production capacity, 

 (b) the production capacity, as determined in accordance with such guiding principles, of the plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments or installations affected by it, 

 (c) the duty or the rate of duty on production capacity, and 

 (d) the manner of collection of such duty. (5) the production capacity of any plant or machinery or part thereof specified in a notification under sub-section (4) shall, upon an application made to the Central Government within thirty days of the notification by any aggrieved person, be reviewed by a Review Board constituted under sub-section (6) to which the application shall be referred; and the decision of the Review Board confirming, reducing or increasing the production capacity shall be final: 

 Provided that, in the case of any plant or machinery used for the manufacture of cotton fabrics or cotton yarn, the production capacity of which was determined before the 30th June, 1970, any aggrieved person may, within such time as the Central Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in this behalf, make an application in writing to the Central Government for re-examination of the production capacity, and such application shall be referred by the Central Government to a special committee constituted for the purpose; and the decision of the special committee on such reference shall be final. 

 (7) The Central Board of Revenue may, by notification in the official Gazette, at any time, cancel a notification under sub-section (4); and where a notification is so cancelled or, for any reason whatsoever, cannot be given effect to the duty under sub-section (1), in lieu whereof the duty under sub-section (4) was levied by such notification, shall be levied and, with necessary adjustment, collected for the financial year during which such notification is cancelled or for the period of which it cannot be given effect to. The expression "excise duty" itself has not been defined in the Act on rules. However, in English law the same "excise" is given to duties of taxes levied on certain articles produced and consumed at home, In the United States jurisdiction, this expression issued to signify imposition, sometimes upon the consumption of commodities, and sometimes upon the retail sales thereof. The scheme of the Central Excise and Salt Act suggests that "excise duty" generally signifies an impost on production of commodities in Pakistan and on services provided and rendered in Pakistan. "Production capacity", according to KG Lockyer in this book entitled Production Control in Practice-1967 Ed." at page 103 defined the expression "Production capacity" to mean the volume of output being capable of production in any convenient time by any plant or installations. The capacity of plant might be viewed from the stand-point of its total maximum output. This is referred to as theoretical or maximum plant capacity. Since even under ideal manufacturing conditions some bottlenecks, delays and other types of production interruptions normally occur; this ideal level of capacity is almost never used to set predetermined overhead rates. Practical plant capacity represents the theoretical capacity less unavoidable timeless." It is not disputed that the duty of excise is leviable on actual production of the excisable goods. The Government had to employ a large number of staffs and machinery for this purpose. This system according to the Law making Authorities is suffered from abuses and grave irregularities and unnecessary complicities. The change in the method of assessment was designed to remove these difficulties and to simplify the procedure for collection of excise duties on actual production, a more simple method was devised, that is, to determine the production capacity of each plant and machinery, etc. and charge excise duty according to the volume of output being capable of production by the industrial unit. 

 12. Sub-section (4) of section 3 invests the Board with the power to levy and collect the excise duties on services but the Board is subjected to certain condition it wants to proceed for levy and collection of the excise duties. The Board has to take prior approval of the Government as to issue notification specifying the guiding principle or determination of such capacity and such guiding principle has to be determined first and thereafter Board should proceed to fix the capacity and rate of the excise duty to be levied. For that purpose the plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments and installations or premises which are likely to be affected by such fixation of capacity that rate be taken into consideration and thereafter such capacity may be determined and the manner of collection of duty may be realized thereafter. Before levy and collection the Board is duty bound to frame the guidelines so that the plants, machinery, undertakings, establishments or installations or premises may not be affected by such fixation. In this respect we may consider the case as referred to by both the parties, namely, Zaibtun Textile Mills Ltd. Karachi and others vs. Central Board of Revenue and others, PLD 1971 Karachi 333. Upon coming into effect the 6th Amendment of the Constitution by which the Central Government was authorized to make law in respect of taxes and duties on production capacity and upon coining into effect of that amendment the Central Government appointed a Committee by a notification dated 12.8.67. The notification provided that the duty on the production capacity of a cotton textile factory as determine by the Committee will be levied under sub-section (4) of section 3 of the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944 and the notified capacity of individual factories would be subject to review on application by the manufacturers, by the Review Board constituted under sub-section (6) of section 3 of the Act. The Committee was constituted with Mr. SB Awan, CSP as Chairman with 3 other members. The guiding principles, to be notified under sub-section (4) of section 3 of the Act, on the basis of which the Committee should determine the production capacity are as follows: 

 "(i) The national annual production of each statutory category of cotton fabrics/cotton yarn on per loom/spindle basis taking production of the past three years into account. 

 (ii) Category-wise annual production of the individual units for the past three years or such lesser period as may be available. 

 (iii) Category-wise annual production of comparable units for the same period. 

 (iv) Production capacity of an individual unit calculated on the basis of the technically possible maximum production potential of the plant and machinery installed in the unit, if it were to aim at maximizing its profits before tax. 

 (v) Growth factor, keeping in view the past rate of improvement in production and likely increase in efficiency relating to improvement in technical, managerial, labour and financial factors of individual mills." 

 13. In the instant case as we have already noticed that the Government has formed no such Committee to frame the guidelines to collect the data to investigate into the condition of the machineries, plants, installations, etc. and the production so made during the time or preceding years. All these conditions were not at all considered in framing the Committee individually as such it cannot be said that the petitioners were heard before making the guidelines as will evidence from the annexures. Section 3(4) of the Act provides that by taking prior approval of the Government the Board may proceed to levy and collect the excise duties on the plants, machineries, undertakings, establishments and installations by issuing any notification and, as such, the notification shall specify the guiding principles for determination of the capacity. If that guiding principles be not framed or made after due application of mind affording opportunity of being heard to the petitioner fixing the rate and determining the capacity will also be liable to be erroneous and the purpose of section 3(4) shall be frustrated. In the case reported in PLD 1971 Karachi 333, we have noticed that the Government by notification formed a High Powered Committee and framed the guidelines who reported to the Government about such finding. 

 14. Mr. AK Mujibur Rahman, the learned Deputy Attorney-General submitted that the SRO so made by the Board are in the nature of Rules. The primary legislative function having ended with amendment giving power to the Board of levy and collect the duties being satisfied with the guiding principles for determination of (he production capacity and that the Board has rightly issued the notifications. As we have already observed that proper care and precaution being not taken in safeguarding the interest of the petitioners by not framing the proper guideline, not taking the maximum arid minimum production capacity of individual plants and installations and working capacity and other inter-related factors, it cannot be said that the guiding principle in law, or in fact, is a proper guiding principle. It is true that the guiding principles are not legislative principles but they are in the nature of rule for the purpose of attaining uniformity in the application of a new provision of the Act to different industrial unit. In our view, the National Board of Revenue has failed to take any precaution to give full details as to how the guidelines are to be framed as the Central Board of Revenue did. We have already stated in-the foregoing paragraphs how the Committee acted in framing the guidelines which has subsequently come into effect. We have also already noticed that although power has been given to the Standing Tribunal constituted under section 3(6) to confirm, reduce or increase the capacity but they failed in their duty in simply saying that the same cannot be granted as the Rules do not provide for such relief.
